protocol.status: Approved by the owner on 25 November 2026 (B = 3000, qa_once kept, six seeds); written and pushed before any stage-76 code or run.
protocol.question: With a cheaper proxy scorer (Qwen2.5-0.5B gradient alignment), on a four-times larger pool at the same QA share (0.25), does a one-pass offline filter that keeps N chunks (mostly QA, each seen once) beat random sampling at equal cost, with the proxy's full scoring time charged?
protocol.motivation: Stage 75: keeping N = 1484 of 2048 chunks removed repetition but diluted the QA share to 0.33 (at most 512 QA chunks exist in that pool); align_once at N minus random at 2400 was -0.033 [-0.086, +0.019]; the throughput term was only +0.022, so the limit was dilution, not cost. Stage-76 smoke 1 (commit 0271ae3): with the full 1.5B scorer (0.444-0.462 random steps per chunk) one view per kept chunk needs a scoring share of at least 0.444 / (0.444 + f) for kept fraction f, so a large pool that the filter could cut to mostly QA is unaffordable. Stage-76 smoke 2 (commit 1f82f72, exposed data only): Qwen2.5-0.5B alignment costs 0.181 random steps per chunk (2.5x cheaper) and separates QA from web at least as well as the full scorer (AUC 0.968/0.973 vs 0.956/0.961; top 256 all QA; top-512 overlap with the full scorer 0.87; Spearman 0.65); last-layer scorers do not separate QA from web (AUC 0.43-0.53) and are excluded.

smoke_tests_before_protocol.smoke_1: commit 0271ae3, tools/smoke_llm_amortized.py, results/llm-amortized-smoke.json: stage-74 pools rebuilt exactly; 5,848 ArabicMMLU test items unscored, untrained and clean under criteria (a)-(e) after excluding the stage-75 target; c_r 0.1102 s; full 1.5B scoring of 2048 chunks 100.3 s (909 random steps); one 512-item evaluation 34.4 s.
smoke_tests_before_protocol.smoke_2: commit 1f82f72, tools/smoke_llm_cheap_scorer.py, results/llm-cheap-scorer-smoke.json: costs and ranking agreement of eight scorers on the stage-74 sigma 0.25 pool against the stage-75 journaled full scores (seeds 37500, 37501, recomputed with difference 0). Qwen2.5-0.5B tokenizer files are byte-identical to the 1.5B ones.
smoke_tests_before_protocol.web_supply: Data-only count before this protocol (no evaluation): with the stage-74 decontamination (any token 8-gram shared with the content of any All/dev or All/test item), 41,443 kept and 18,831 removed FineWeb-2 chunks are eligible (637 and 356 dropped), as stage 74.

protocol.hardware: The Colab NVIDIA L4 of this session; device journaled with the calibration; resuming on a different device type aborts; resuming on another L4 is allowed with the journaled calibration (no recalibration), as stages 74-75.
protocol.model: Trained model as stages 73-75: Qwen2.5-1.5B (revision 8faed76 and SHA-256 as research/llm-gpu-scale-protocol.json), float32, deterministic algorithms, TF32 off, LoRA rank 8 alpha 16 on q_proj and v_proj, AdamW lr 5e-4 weight decay 0, one 65-token chunk per update. Proxy scorer model: Qwen2.5-0.5B (revision 060db649 and SHA-256 as research/llm-gpu-scale-protocol.json), same numerics and LoRA, used for scoring only. transformers 4.46.3, tokenizers 0.20.3, huggingface_hub 0.26.2; torch 2.14.1+cu130.

data.qa_chunks: The 2048 in-format QA chunks of stage 74 (experiments.llm_qa_mix.qa_list, the sigma 1.0 pilot pool, pool digest 12b3a1f8...): every item in them is among the 4,946 IDs already recorded as used for training; no new ArabicMMLU item is trained. The first 512 are the QA chunks of the stage-74/75 sigma 0.25 pool.
data.web_chunks: From the stage-74 decontaminated chunk lists (first 65 tokens of each document with at least 65 tokens, in file order; same files, hashes and decontamination): 3072 kept chunks drawn by default_rng(7611).choice(41443, 3072, replace=False) and 3072 removed chunks by default_rng(7612).choice(18831, 3072, replace=False), in draw order. Counts must equal 41,443 and 18,831, else abort.
data.pool: M = 8192 chunks: positions 0-2047 the QA chunks, 2048-5119 the kept web chunks, 5120-8191 the removed web chunks (QA share 0.25, web half kept, half removed, as stage 74). Pool SHA-256 journaled with the calibration.
data.probe: All 120 All/dev items (already exposed; the alignment target of the proxy; not used for any claim).

task.format: ArabicMMLU cloze, item loss (mean NLL of the correct continuation) and accuracy exactly as stages 73-75 (experiments.llm_web_filter.evaluate), with the 1.5B model.
task.target_eligibility: ArabicMMLU All/test rows that are (1) not the stage-73 target, the stage-74 pilot, the stage-74 target or the stage-75 target, (2) not one of the 4,946 IDs used for training, and (3) clean under criteria (a)-(e) of stage 75 (experiments.llm_once_filter.target_candidates, unchanged), with criterion (e) applied to the stage-76 pool as trained (all 8192 chunks) plus the 4,946 items tokenized in the training template. Counts journaled; abort if fewer than 512 rows are eligible.
task.target: 512 items: default_rng(7622).choice over the eligible rows (in row order), sorted. Never evaluated before; exposed after this stage.

design.budget: B = 3000 random-step costs. Calibration before any target evaluation, seed 76999 on the stage-76 pool: c_r = median of steps 5-24 of 24 random 1.5B steps; S = wall-clock of complete proxy scoring of all 8192 chunks (0.5B model loaded with LoRA at the seed, probe gradient included; experiments.llm_web_filter.score, align_grad, batch 16). N = floor(B - S / c_r + 1e-9). Expected S about 1,490 random steps (linear extrapolation of smoke 2) and N about 1,510. Abort unless 1000 <= N <= 2048 (qa_once needs N distinct QA chunks).

arms.random: Each step a pool chunk drawn uniformly with replacement; 3000 updates.
arms.align05_once: Score all 8192 chunks with the 0.5B proxy at the seed's initial adapter (the proxy model is freed before the 1.5B model is loaded); keep the N highest scores (ties to the lower index); train the 1.5B model on the kept chunks in a random order without replacement (one pass by step N; further passes freshly permuted up to 3000). The proxy's full scoring time is charged.
arms.random_once: Repetition-matched control: a uniformly random N-chunk subset of the pool with the align05_once order. No scoring, no charge.
arms.qa_once: Label oracle (secondary, uncharged): a uniformly random N-chunk subset of the 2048 QA chunks with the align05_once order. Separates ranking quality from finding QA; it uses the pool labels, which a real filter does not have.

design.scoring: Proxy scores are computed once per seed in the align05_once run and journaled with the kept indices and the QA share. They are deterministic given the seed.
design.schedule: Per seed: rng = default_rng(seed); in this order: rand = rng.integers(8192, size=3000); subsetN = sort(rng.choice(8192, N, replace=False)); qaN = sort(rng.choice(2048, N, replace=False)); once = concatenate of ceil(3000 / N) successive rng.permutation(N), truncated to 3000. align05_once trains keptN[once], random_once subsetN[once], qa_once qaN[once], random rand.
design.run_order: Seeds in order; arms in the order (random, align05_once, random_once, qa_once) rotated left by the seed index mod 4.
design.measurement: Every arm trains 3000 updates; target loss and accuracy at 0, N and 3000. Per align05_once run: all 8192 scores, kept indices and digest, QA share of the kept set, scoring seconds. Per control: subset digest and QA share. Views per training-set chunk at N and 3000 (max and mean) for every arm. Step seconds per update; adapter digest at step 50 for every arm.
design.coverage: 6 seeds x 4 arms = 24 runs plus one calibration; about 3.5 h on this L4 (24 x about 434 s + 6 x about 180 s of proxy scoring + calibration, data and target eligibility about 15 min).

protocol.primary: align05_once loss at N minus random loss at 3000 (equal cost, proxy scoring charged), mean over six seeds, paired seed-bootstrap 95% interval (seed 7603, 10000 resamples). Negative favours the filter.
protocol.secondary: Paired seed-bootstrap intervals, no multiplicity adjustment: (1) selection at matched repetition: align05_once at N minus random_once at N; (2) ranking quality: align05_once at N minus qa_once at N; (3) label-oracle bound: qa_once at N minus random at 3000; (4) one-view effect: random_once at N minus random at N; (5) selection and throughput terms (align05_once at N minus random at N; primary minus that); (6) amortized contrast at 3000 (align05_once then in later passes); (7) accuracy versions of the primary and (1); (8) QA share of the align05_once kept sets and of the random_once subsets; QA chunks drawn and distinct QA chunks seen by random at N and 3000; (9) random at 3000 minus no update.

prediction.written: Before any stage-76 code or run, 25 November 2026.
prediction.reasoning: With N about 1,510 and 2048 QA chunks among 8192, the proxy (top 256 all QA, AUC about 0.97 on the stage-74 pool) should keep mostly QA, so align05_once sees about 1,300-1,450 distinct QA chunks once. Random at 3000 draws about 750 QA chunks (about 630 distinct) and about 2,250 web chunks. In stage 75 the extra web updates of random added little (+0.022 between N and 2400), and loss fell with the number of distinct QA chunks seen once. A crude linear extrapolation of the small stage-75 differences gives a primary of about -0.05 to -0.15; this magnitude is speculative and not part of the tested prediction.
items: QA share of the align05_once kept sets > 0.85 (pool 0.25).
Primary: align05_once at N minus random at 3000 is negative.
align05_once at N minus random_once at N is negative.
align05_once at N minus qa_once at N is non-negative (the label oracle is no worse than the proxy).
prediction.what_would_refute: A primary contrast >= 0 means that, even when a cheap filter can keep mostly in-format QA seen once, the update budget given up for scoring outweighs the selection gain on this pool; a QA share near 0.25 would instead mean the proxy ranking does not transfer to the larger pool.

protocol.resumption: Append-only JSON-lines journal outside the repository (/content/stage76-journal/journal.jsonl); completed (seed, arm) entries skipped; population, target, pool and schedule digests re-verified on restart; outcomes not printed or read before the run finishes. After every finished run (and after the calibration) the runner copies the journal and run log to branch colab/stage76-journal (results/stage76-interim/), commits and pushes; on a failed push it logs git's stderr and retries the push once before continuing (stage-75 deviation 1). The commit message counts only entries of kind 'run'. Not on main.
protocol.audit: tools/audit_llm_cheap_filter.py: journal digest; summary recomputation; environments; calibration and N; run grid and order; schedules and subset digests; checkpoints; kept sets recomputed from journaled scores; views per chunk from the schedules; QA shares; data and model hashes (both models); pool rebuilt and its digest; QA chunks equal the stage-74 sigma 1.0 pool QA; target eligibility recomputed (criteria (a)-(e) and counts), target disjoint from all exposed and trained IDs. On the same GPU type: recompute the proxy scores of seed 37600; replay the first 50 steps of seed 37600 for random and align05_once to their adapter digests.
protocol.exposure: After the run, data/evaluation_status.json records the 512 stage-76 target items as evaluated and exposed. No new ArabicMMLU item is trained; 6,144 FineWeb-2 chunks are trained, recorded by their document indices.
protocol.licenses: As stages 74-75: FineWeb-2 ODC-By 1.0; ArabicMMLU CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial research use); Qwen2.5 Apache-2.0. No dataset text is committed; journals hold indices, scores and digests only.
protocol.scope: One trained model, one proxy, LoRA, one budget (3000), one pool (QA share 0.25, M = 8192), kept size N, one task scored by answer loss. As in stages 74-75 the QA chunks come from the target's own distribution and template, so a win measures finding target-distribution data hidden in web noise at equal cost, not a general capability gain. The proxy's cost advantage (2.5x) was measured on this L4 and may differ on other hardware.

primary.contrast: align05_once at N minus random at 3000
